channel.title: News Officina
channel.description: Independent. These outlets are written with AI from public sources; one editor reads and approves what goes out. Each says how it is made on its own About page.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: EU and Canada launch Alliance for the Future, covering security
item.description: Canada becomes the first non-European country in the EU's Safe defence procurement scheme, with contracts already won by Canadian firms in Poland and Latvia.

item.title: Europa Surgit: EU and Canada launch Alliance for the Future with defence deal
item.description: Canada becomes the first non-European participant in the EU's Safe defence procurement scheme, and the EU says the model could extend to Japan, South Korea and Australia.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: French minister accuses Mélenchon of speaking for the Kremlin over Donbas vote
item.description: Jean-Noël Barrot says the vote plan would merely repeat Putin's justification for the war, and rejects claims that aid to Ukraine is to blame for French purchasing-power problems.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: Six reported dead and 16 wounded after man opens fire on Krakow's Main Market Square
item.description: Police overpowered the 24-year-old after a gun fight, and prosecutors say the same investigation covers three killings in his home town. Karol Nawrocki has declared two days of national mourning.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: Colau plans 2% tax on wealth over a million euros
item.description: Her Frente Amplio says the Barcelona plan would push more than 500,000 homes back onto the market. Rents hit by it would fall 31% on average.

item.title: Europa Surgit: Hoarded homes are a European failure, not a Spanish one
item.description: Thirteen funds own 100,000 homes in Spain, and a country is reaching for expropriation because the market outgrew it. Europe should finance affordable rental supply before every capital improvises its own drastic law.

item.title: Europa Patriarum: Seven parliaments legislating is not fragmentation. It is consent
item.description: Brussels wants one rulebook for addictive design, replacing laws that seven nations are already passing. A floor of minimum harmonisation we could accept. A regulation that wipes national law hands power to an institution no European voter can remove.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: Prices won the election. Europe still has no shield for port pay.
item.description: The tariffs that squeeze our freight and shifts survived the midterms untouched, because no Congress gets a vote on them. The Commission and member states owe port workers a costed plan before year end.

item.title: Europa Surgit: Parliament to vote in December on proposed pesticide Omnibus
item.description: The Council wants unlimited approvals limited to low-risk substances, while 550 scientists urge suspension and EFSA says about 50 more experts would cut reassessment delays.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: One Polish court now has two managements and neither has given way
item.description: A weekend order replaced the Constitutional Tribunal's leadership, but only two of the six judges elected by the Sejm have taken their oaths. The dispute over who controls the court will turn on those oaths and on whether any EU move goes beyond statements.

item.title: Nuntii Batavi: Plan the Dutch defence budget as if the American cheque never arrives
item.description: Congress authorises the money, the president decides whether it moves, and this year showed which half wins. The cabinet should stop writing American funds and troops into our planning as if they were certain.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: Nobody in Washington will pay for Europe's defence
item.description: The midterms confirm what was already true: Congress controls little that matters, earmarked money is intent rather than commitment, and the Pentagon is expected to hand Europe's defence to Europe. Member states should budget as if American money were not coming.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Voters punished the man who taxed their prices. Europe must answer tariffs with one voice
item.description: Section 301 lets the US president tax European trade with no vote by lawmakers, and the election changed nothing about that power. Every government that cuts its own deal spends the strongest card Europe holds.

item.title: Europa Patriarum: American law binds no president. National law must bind Europe's defence.
item.description: An 86-vote sanctions act sat unused after an October waiver, and 400 million dollars authorized by Congress was delayed. A Congress that can be read around is not a guarantee; only national statutes are.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Kallas says Europe will refuse to implement any Ukraine deal it did not join
item.description: Washington and Moscow keep negotiating in formats with no seat for Europe, while Meloni asks the December summit to pick a single negotiator. Kallas said any agreement must stop Russia using a pause to rearm.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Meta, Google and TikTok sue to block California ban on addictive feeds for under-16s
item.description: The companies filed suit on November 4 against Assembly Bill 1709, which they call a violation of free speech. Attorney General Rob Bonta's office says it will defend the law in court.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Belgrade judge detains special police commander on torture suspicion
item.description: The head of Serbia's SAJ unit faces up to 30 days in detention over the alleged torture of ten people in a government garage. The Belgrade Bar Association says the timing of arrests at the close of the election campaign raises suspicion of political use of police and prosecutors.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Congress moves to impeach Hegseth as Trump defends his secretary over Iran war
item.description: Representative Thomas Massie is preparing to force a vote on impeachment. Republicans had knives out after a $47 billion Iran war the Washington Post says doomed the party.

item.title: Europae Laeva: House vote looms on impeaching US defence secretary Pete Hegseth over Iran war
item.description: Representative Thomas Massie plans to force the vote next week, and President Trump says he intends to keep his defence secretary. The war has cost $47 billion.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Iraq proposes regional ministers' committee as oil losses pass $60bn in US-Iran war
item.description: Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein says the committee would visit Tehran and Washington to seek calm. Iraq has lost $60bn, about €54 billion, since Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz, which carries 90 percent of its oil exports.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: SAJ commander Igor Žmirić held for up to 30 days over torture claims
item.description: The Belgrade court ordered detention of the police unit chief, who faces suspicion of abuse and torture. Lawyers say the arrests before the elections look political; the chief prosecutor denies it.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: Dutch security report says AI now used at every stage of cyber attacks
item.description: The NCTV warns it is a matter of when, not whether, the Netherlands faces a society-disrupting incident, and names China, Russia, Iran and North Korea as threats.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Iraq proposes ministerial shuttle between Tehran and Washington as losses pass $60bn
item.description: Oil revenues lost since February 2026 equal about €54 billion, and oil funds roughly 90 percent of the federal budget. Foreign minister Fuad Hussein's plan follows Iranian terms for resuming talks, including reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Leo Batavus: Hackers use AI in every attack phase, NCTV warns
item.description: The NCTV says a disruptive attack on Dutch society is a matter of when, not whether, in its yearly threat report published on Friday. The cabinet answered with a new action programme the same day.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Belgrade court detains police commander over garage torture case
item.description: Belgrade judges ordered SAJ commander Igor Žmirić held for up to 30 days with eight other suspects, while bar association president Vladimir Prijovic says the timing of arrests raises suspicion that police and prosecutors serve political ends.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Commission puts mandatory migration solidarity to the Council's decision
item.description: The Solidarity Pool for 2027 would let member states pay €20,000 per person not relocated, but contributions bind only once the Council agrees, and Hungary and Slovakia pledged nothing for 2026.

item.title: Europa Surgit: Commission proposes secret 2027 solidarity pool as EU relocations fall short
item.description: EU governments relocated fewer than 9,000 asylum seekers in 2026 against an agreed figure of 21,000, and the Council must now set each country's share by the end of next year.

item.title: Europa Surgit: Europe earned a seat at the Ukraine talks. One negotiator can take it.
item.description: Moscow set the guest list, and Europe still has no one to send. On 13 November EU leaders must name a single negotiator with a standing mandate, before the next round opens.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: Male State founder denies involvement in European flight bomb threats
item.description: Vladislav Pozdniakov said on Telegram that the far-right group no longer exists, as alerts again disrupted flights on 6 November. The Rome Prosecutor's Office has opened an investigation.

item.title: Leo Batavus: Meta, Google and TikTok sue to block California ban on teen feeds
item.description: The three companies filed separate lawsuits on November 4 against Assembly Bill 1709, which takes effect on January 1, 2027. Attorney General Rob Bonta says his office will defend the law.
